A couple of things you can do to get the best fuel economy:

(1) Make sure your tires are inflated to the pressure listed on the label in your door jamb. Under inflated tires increase rolling resistance, reducing fuel economy. So will oversized tires.

(2) have your wheel alignment checked. If your vehicle is out of alignment, it will increase rolling resistance.

(3) Make sure your brake components are all working properly. If a brake is dragging, it can reduce fuel economy. On this model the rear brake caliper slides often freeze, which can cause rear brake pads to not release completely.

(4) One thing that will dramatically affect your fuel economy is the ethanol content of the fuel you are using. All gasoline sold at the pumps in the US is blended with some amount of ethanol. Ethanol does not contain as much energy as straight gasoline; the more alcohol in the blend the fewer miles you will get to a tank full of fuel. Even though pumps may be labelled 10% ethanol, the actual amount in the blend van vary widely from one brand to another. You can measure the amount of ethanol in your fuel (the procedure can be found on the EPA web site), or you can try switching to a different brand of fuel to see if it affects your gas mileage.

(5) You may want to ask your mechanic to check your engine control system for any possible faults that can affect fuel economy. For example, if your engine is running slightly below temperature because of an out of calibration thermostat the computer will command a richer fuel mixture because it thinks the engine is still warming up; this will use more fuel. If you have a degraded oxygen sensor, or an aftermarket one from a discount parts supplier, that can cause a richer than normal fuel mixture also. A torque converter that is not going into lockup will drop gas mileage a couple mpg, so will a transmission that is slipping or not going into high gear. Low engine vacuum will cause a rich fuel mixture. Checking for these types of causes does require some special test equipment and a working knowledge of engine control systems though, so you may not be able to check all of these things yourself at home.
